result.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
result.summary: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). Trained on the same navigation episodes, ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on standard VLN-CE (continuous environments) benchmarks, while inducing only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserving its general capabilities. To our knowledge, ZeroVLN is the first slow-fast VLN framework with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain, and the first to jointly optimize its slow and fast policies through closed-loop agentic RL in VLN-CE.

AI.brief_summary: ZeroVLN 提出 slow-fast 视觉语言导航框架：不对 VLM「大脑」做导航域 SFT，而以自然语言语义工具调用接口把移动决策交给 action expert，再用闭环强化学习联合优化慢决策与快执行。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保持基座 VLM 权重大体不变、只训练轻量执行端」的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉能力退化与信息坍缩、以及慢推理与快执行的贡献分配提供可核查线索；任务本身属机器人导航，与 latent 推理状态无直接关联。
